import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_16/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_16/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_16/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
join_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above result on user_id
join_0_1_2 = pd.merge(source0, join_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by title and compute average rating filtered by gender
# avg(Source3_16_1.rating) filtered by gender='F' as F
# avg(Source3_16_1.rating) filtered by gender='M' as M

# Filter ratings by gender and group by title
f_ratings = join_0_1_2[join_0_1_2["gender"] == "F"].groupby("title")["rating"].mean()
m_ratings = join_0_1_2[join_0_1_2["gender"] == "M"].groupby("title")["rating"].mean()

# Combine the two series into a dataframe
result = pd.DataFrame({
    "F": f_ratings,
    "M": m_ratings
}).reset_index()

# Ensure columns are in the order: ['title', 'F', 'M']
result = result[["title", "F", "M"]]

# Write the result to the target path
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_16_0 and Source3_16_1 on user_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_16_2 on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating grouped by title and gender
# Pivot the gender to columns F and M with average ratings
# First, filter ratings by gender and aggregate

# Group by title and gender, compute average rating
grouped = joined_all.groupby(['title', 'gender'], as_index=False)['rating'].mean()

# Pivot gender to columns F and M
pivoted = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivoted = pivoted.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Ensure columns order as in target schema
pivoted = pivoted[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Write output to target file
pivoted.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
